# Fixture sources (FSD C-08)

Every committed fixture: where it comes from, its licence, and how to rebuild
it. Fixture paths are relative to `tests/integration`, in unblob's
integration layout `<category>/<name>/__input__` (FSD C-09). All fixtures below are generated by `tests/fixtures/build.sh` inside the
devcontainer image from one payload, so they carry no third-party content.

**Expected output (C-09):** each `__input__` has the `__output__` that
`python -m tests.integration.build_outputs` writes (unblob with this package
loaded, extracted as unblob's `test_all_handlers` does); TC-CON-14 compares
against it. `executable/nsis/__output__` is empty (`.gitkeep`) because the
pinned unblob has no NSIS handler yet; it fills when #1255 lands (D-1).

**Payload:** `payload.py`, 4 KiB: the tag `UIH-FIXTURE-v1` followed by
SHA-256 counter-mode bytes from a fixed seed. A match in extracted output
cannot occur by chance.

**Licence:** MIT (this repository). Redistributable under unblob's test suite.

**Rebuild:** `tests/fixtures/build.sh`. Output is reproducible: two builds
give identical files, except `archive/mcuboot/__input__/encrypted.bin` (see its row). The script checks each fixture against its oracle
(FSD §16.1) before printing its hash.

| Fixture | Built with | Content | Oracle check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `archive/uf2/__input__/standard.uf2` | `uf2conv.py` (microsoft/uf2 `90e9741`) | payload at `0x10000000`, family RP2040 `0xe48bff56` | UF2 → bin round trip identical |
| `archive/ihex/__input__/standard.hex` | `avr-objcopy` (binutils-avr 2.43.50) | payload at `0x08000000` | HEX → bin round trip identical |
| `archive/dfuse/__input__/standard.dfu` | `dfuse-pack.py` (dfu-util 0.11) | one target, one element at `0x08000000`, VID/PID `0483:df11` | `dfu-suffix -c` accepts suffix and CRC |
| `archive/mcuboot/__input__/standard.bin` | `imgtool` 2.5.0 | header 0x20, version `1.2.3+4`, unsigned (hash TLV only) | `imgtool verify` passes; image bytes equal the payload |
| `archive/mcuboot/__input__/encrypted.bin` | `imgtool` 2.5.0, `-E` with a throwaway X25519 key | as `standard.bin`, image AES-128 encrypted (ENCX25519 TLV); **not reproducible**: the AES key is random per build, so the committed bytes are the fixture | `imgtool dumpinfo` reports `ENCRYPTED_AES128`; image bytes differ from the payload |
| `archive/mcuboot/__input__/protected.bin` | `imgtool` 2.5.0, `--security-counter 7` | as `standard.bin`, plus a protected TLV area (SEC_CNT) at `0x1020` with magic `0x6908` | `imgtool dumpinfo` shows a protected TLV area |
| `archive/installshield/__input__/standard.cab` | `installshield_cab.py` (this repository, MIT), layout as unshield 1.6.2 reads it | version 5 cabinet: file group `Firmware`, directory `app`, `firmware.bin` (the payload, compressed) and `readme.txt` (stored) | `unshield x` 1.6.2 extracts both; `firmware.bin` identical to the payload |
| `archive/installshield/__input__/set.tar` | `installshield_cab.py --set` (this repository, MIT) | the same cabinet as a version 5 set: `set/data1.hdr` (headers and descriptor) and `set/data1.cab` (zero-size descriptor and the data), tar metadata fixed | `unshield x` on `data1.hdr` extracts `firmware.bin` identical |
| `executable/nsis/__input__/standard.exe` | `makensis` 3.10 (`standard.nsi`), build time pinned | installs the payload as `firmware.bin` | `7z e` extracts `firmware.bin` identical to the payload |

## Text corpus (FR-HEX-02)

`archive/ihex/text-corpus/__input__/fields.rst`, `archive/ihex/text-corpus/__input__/settings.py.txt` (Python dict
literals; `.txt` keeps it out of the linters), `archive/ihex/text-corpus/__input__/device.log` and
`archive/ihex/text-corpus/__input__/board.yaml`: written by hand for this repository (MIT), no build
step. Non-HEX text whose lines
start with or contain `:` followed by hex digits, including an EOF-like
`:00000001FF`. Oracle: none needed; the expected result is no `ihex` chunk.

## Inno Setup

Built by `tests/fixtures/build-inno.sh` from `standard.iss` (cut down from the
Script Wizard template in
[gist m-biernat/45dfe849…](https://gist.github.com/m-biernat/45dfe8494916e2d2f4fae408caaea3b1)).
Each installer is compiled by that Inno version's own `ISCC.exe`, extracted
with innoextract from the official installer, and run under Wine 10.0 in a
throwaway container. Installers made with Inno Setup may be redistributed
freely (Inno Setup licence); the payload is ours (MIT).

| Fixture | Compiler (source, sha256) | Setup data version | Oracle check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `executable/inno/__input__/standard-5.6.1-unicode.exe` | files.jrsoftware.org/is/5/innosetup-5.6.1-unicode.exe (`27d49e9b…b538`) | 5.6.0 (unicode) | innoextract yields `firmware.bin` identical to the payload |
| `executable/inno/__input__/standard-6.1.2.exe` | jrsoftware/issrc release is-6_1_2 (`a3ce1c40…35e7`) | 6.1.0 | same |
| `executable/inno/__input__/standard-6.4.3.exe` | is-6_4_3 (`f3c42116…723b`) | 6.4.3 | same |
| `executable/inno/__input__/standard-6.7.3.exe` | is-6_7_3 (`9c73c3ba…b732`) | 6.7.0 | same |
| `executable/inno/__input__/standard-7.1.0.exe` | is-7_1_0, x86 (`f9671174…4f60`) | 7.0.0.3 | same | <!-- scrub:allow version number -->

**Not byte-reproducible.** Two builds differ in about 21 bytes inside the setup
header (a build-time value and its checksum); size and extracted contents are
identical. The committed bytes are the fixture; rebuild only to add a version.

**Wine is a temporary build tool.** It is used by this script alone, during
development (user decision 2026-10-24). When it is removed, regenerating these
fixtures needs Windows (any machine with Inno Setup's ISCC.exe).

## WiX/Burn

`executable/wix_burn/__input__/standard.exe` is built by `tests/fixtures/build-burn.sh`. The script runs
WiX 3.14.1 (`wix314-binaries.zip`, sha256 `6ac824e1…3d31`) under Wine 10.0 with
Wine Mono 9.4.0 (`cf6173ae…cacb2`), in a throwaway container:
- `burn-fixture.wxs` becomes an MSI that installs the payload as `firmware.bin`;
- `burn-bundle.wxs` chains that MSI into a Burn bundle using
  WixStandardBootstrapperApplication.

**Licence.** WiX is MS-RL; bundles it produces may be redistributed. The
payload is ours (MIT).

**Oracle check.** The bundle has a `.wixburn` section and two CAB containers:
UX `u0…`, and attached `a0`. `a0` is the MSI (magic `d0 cf 11 e0`), and the MSI
yields `FirmwareBin` identical to the payload.

**Not byte-reproducible.** WiX generates package GUIDs and timestamps, so the
size varies by a few bytes. The committed bytes are the fixture.

## Not sourced

- **InstallShield, version 6 and later.** Only the version 5 cabinet is
  written by hand (`installshield_cab.py`); building a v6+ set needs
  InstallShield, which is commercial and Windows-only. Sets are verified on
  real files only.
- **Setup Factory.** No redistributable sample. The only one is a Setup
  Factory 10.4 trial build in the real-file store (`setup-factory-sample`),
  so the handler is verified on real files only.
